A_target.statement:
Let $a \ge 1$, $b > 1$, $c > 0$, $d \ge 0$ and $\map T n = a \map T {n / b} + c n^d$ for $n$ a power of $b$, with $\map T 1 = \map \Theta 1$.
Then:
:$\map T n = \begin {cases} \map \Theta {n^d} & : d > \log_b a \\ \map \Theta {n^d \log n} & : d = \log_b a \\ \map \Theta {n^{\log_b a} } & : d < \log_b a \end {cases}$

B_source.statement:
Let $r > 0$.
Then $\displaystyle \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^k r^j$ is $\map \Theta 1$ if $r < 1$, equal to $k + 1$ if $r = 1$, and $\map \Theta {r^k}$ if $r > 1$, as $k \to \infty$.

substitutions.the number of terms: the depth log_b n of the recursion tree

derived.the three regimes of the geometric sum: the three cases of the master theorem

object_map.reformulation: Unroll the recurrence into a recursion tree whose level costs form a geometric sequence.

validity_conditions: Restricting to powers of b avoids rounding; monotonicity extends the result.
The leaves contribute a^(log_b n) = n^(log_b a), which matches the third case.
proof_plan: At depth $j$ of the recursion tree there are $a^j$ subproblems of size $n / b^j$, costing in total $c \, a^j \paren {n / b^j}^d = c n^d r^j$ with $r = \dfrac a {b^d}$.
The depth is $\log_b n$, and the leaves contribute $a^{\log_b n} \map T 1 = \map \Theta {n^{\log_b a} }$.
Hence $\map T n = c n^d \displaystyle \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^{\log_b n - 1} r^j + \map \Theta {n^{\log_b a} }$.

By the source result: if $r < 1$, that is $d > \log_b a$, the total is $\map \Theta {n^d}$; if $r = 1$ it is $\map \Theta {n^d \log n}$; if $r > 1$ it is $\map \Theta {n^d r^{\log_b n} } = \map \Theta {n^{\log_b a} }$.
{{qed}}
